scenario: A processor executes computer instructions
question: Which CPU component interprets and executes instructions from memory?
guidance: Students should know CPU component functions

points: B - Control Unit coordinates instruction execution
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: CU is the 'director' of CPU operations

scenario: A processor performs mathematical calculations
question: What does the ALU do in a CPU?
options: B) Performs arithmetic and logic operations

points: B - ALU performs arithmetic and logic operations
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: ALU handles calculations and comparisons

scenario: CPU registers hold data during processing
question: What are CPU registers and explain why they are important.
guidance: Should explain register purpose and benefit

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for definition, 1 for importance
points: Definition: Very fast temporary storage locations within CPU
Importance: Hold data being actively processed
Importance: Fastest memory access type
Importance: Enable quick calculations without memory delay
Importance: Critical for CPU performance
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on speed and immediate access benefits
mark_scheme.do_not_accept: 'Storage in CPU' without explaining speed advantage

scenario: A computer needs memory for running applications
question: What is RAM used for?
options: B) Temporary storage while programs are running

points: B - RAM is temporary volatile memory for running programs
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: RAM clears when power off
mark_scheme.do_not_accept: Permanent storage or other memory types

scenario: A computer needs firmware to boot up
question: What is ROM and what is stored in it?
guidance: Should explain ROM purpose and contents

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for definition, 1 for content
points: Definition: Read-Only Memory - permanent non-volatile memory
Content: BIOS (firmware needed to start computer)
Content: Boot instructions
Content: Permanent system data
Cannot be changed under normal use
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on permanent nature and boot function

scenario: CPU cache improves performance for frequently accessed data
question: Explain why cache memory improves CPU performance.

points: Cache is much faster than main RAM
Stores frequently accessed data close to CPU
Reduces need to fetch from slower main memory
Speeds up instruction execution
Very fast but limited in size
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on speed comparison with main memory

scenario: A CPU specification shows clock speed of 3.6 GHz
question: What does clock speed measure?
options: A) Amount of RAM in gigabytes
B) Number of instructions executed per second
guidance: Students should understand clock speed significance

points: B - Clock speed is frequency of processor cycles per second
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Higher GHz = more cycles per second

scenario: A computer upgrade considers replacing HDD with SSD
question: Describe the key differences between HDD and SSD storage.
guidance: Should contrast mechanical vs electronic storage

points: HDD: Uses spinning magnetic disks and mechanical read/write heads
SSD: Uses flash memory (no moving parts)
HDD: Slower but more affordable, larger capacity
SSD: Much faster but more expensive, smaller capacity
HDD: More likely to fail from physical damage
SSD: More reliable with no moving parts
SSD: Draws less power, quieter operation
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on technology difference and performance tradeoff

scenario: Legacy data is stored on CD or DVD disks
question: Which of these is an example of optical storage?
guidance: Students should know storage device types

points: B - DVD is optical storage using laser to read data
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Also accepts CD, Blu-ray as optical

scenario: User inputs text and commands via keyboard
question: What is the main purpose of a keyboard?

points: To input text, numbers, and commands into computer
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Primary text input device

scenario: User navigates graphical interface with mouse
question: What does a mouse detect to move the cursor?
guidance: Students should know mouse input method

points: B - Mouse detects movement and clicks
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Creates visual cursor movement on screen

scenario: Paper documents are converted to digital format
question: What does a scanner do and what input does it accept?

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for function, 1 for input type
points: Function: Converts physical documents into digital images/data
Input: Accepts paper documents
Input: Can scan photographs, text, graphics
Creates digital file from physical original
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on image/document capture

scenario: User records audio or uses voice commands
question: What type of input does a microphone accept?
guidance: Students should know microphone input type

points: B - Microphone accepts sound/audio input
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Converts sound waves to digital signal

scenario: Information is displayed on computer screen
question: What is the purpose of a monitor and what key specification affects image quality?
guidance: Should explain display function and resolution

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for purpose, 1 for specification
points: Purpose: Displays visual output from computer to user
Specification: Resolution (pixel count) affects clarity
Specification: Refresh rate affects smoothness
Specification: Size and screen type (LCD, LED, etc.)
Higher resolution = sharper image
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on visual display and resolution impact

scenario: User needs physical copies of documents
question: Which of these is a printer type?

points: C - Laser printer is a type of output device
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Also accept inkjet, thermal, dot matrix

scenario: Office needs to decide between inkjet and laser printer
question: Explain the differences between inkjet and laser printers. Which is better for high-volume printing?

mark_scheme.instruction: Award marks for comparison and recommendation
points: Inkjet: Sprays liquid ink onto paper, slower, cheaper upfront
Laser: Uses toner cartridge and heat, faster, higher per-unit cost
Inkjet: Lower cost per page for occasional use
Laser: Lower cost per page for high-volume printing
Laser: Better for business/office use with high volume
Inkjet: Better for home/photo printing
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Award marks for clear comparison and justified recommendation

scenario: Audio output is needed from a computer
question: What type of output do speakers provide?
guidance: Students should know output device types

points: B - Speakers convert digital audio to sound waves
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Audio output device

scenario: Motherboard contains all main computer components
question: What is a motherboard and name two components connected to it.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for definition, 1 for components
points: Definition: Main circuit board connecting all computer components
Components: CPU socket, RAM slots, expansion cards
Components: Storage controllers, power connectors
Components: BIOS chip, chipset
Components: PCI slots, USB headers
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Award marks for defining circuit board function and any two components

scenario: Data travels through computer via buses
question: What is a bus in computer architecture? Name one type of bus.
guidance: Should define and identify bus type

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for definition, 1 for bus type
points: Definition: Pathway for data transmission between components
Type: Address bus - carries memory addresses
Type: Data bus - carries actual data
Type: Control bus - carries control signals
Buses coordinate component communication
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Award marks for definition and any correct bus type

scenario: CPU needs to access specific memory location
question: What does the address bus carry?

points: B - Address bus specifies which memory location to access
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Width of address bus determines addressable memory

scenario: Data is transferred between components
question: What is the purpose of the data bus?
options: B) Carry actual data between components
guidance: Students should understand data bus function

points: B - Data bus transfers actual data/instructions
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Width (bits) determines amount of data transferred at once

scenario: Components must coordinate timing and operations
question: Describe what the control bus does in a computer.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for control bus explanation
points: Carries control signals coordinating component operations
Signals include: read/write commands, interrupt signals
Coordinates timing of data transfers
Manages interaction between CPU, memory, I/O devices
Enables synchronization of operations
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on coordination and control function

scenario: Digital computers work with binary numbers
question: Explain what binary is and why computers use it.
guidance: Should define binary and explain computer relevance

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for definition, 1 for computer use reason
points: Definition: Number system using base 2 (digits 0 and 1)
Reason: Computer circuits use on/off states (1/0)
Reason: Binary directly maps to electronic states
Reason: Simpler than decimal for electronic representation
All computer data ultimately represented as binary
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on on/off electronic nature explanation

scenario: Converting between number systems
question: Convert the binary number 1011 to denary (decimal).

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for correct answer, 1 for working
points: Answer: 11 (denary)
Award mark for showing positional value calculation
Award mark for correct final answer
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Accept working shown in different notation

scenario: Converting decimal number to binary
question: Convert the denary number 25 to binary.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for working, 1 for answer
points: Answer: 11001
Working: 25 ÷ 2 = 12 rem 1, 12 ÷ 2 = 6 rem 0, etc.
Award for either division or powers of 2 method
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Accept either division or powers of 2 approach

scenario: Data storage uses bits and bytes as units
question: How many bits are in one byte?
guidance: Students should know basic data units

points: C - 1 byte = 8 bits
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Fundamental data unit measurement

scenario: Understanding file and storage sizes
question: Describe the relationship between kilobyte, megabyte, and gigabyte.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark per correct unit relationship
points: 1 KB = 1,024 bytes (approximately 1,000)
Each unit is 1,024 times larger than previous
OR approximately 1,000 times for simplification
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Award marks for showing progression/relationships

scenario: Determining storage requirements
question: An image is 2.5 MB. How many images of this size can fit on a USB drive with 2 GB capacity?
guidance: Should show calculation with unit conversion

points: Convert 2 GB to MB: 2 × 1024 = 2048 MB
Answer: 819 complete images (rounded down)
Award 1 mark for unit conversion
Award 1 mark for division
Award 1 mark for correct final answer
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Accept either 1,000 or 1,024 multiplier if clearly stated

scenario: Determining system memory requirements
question: If a computer has 8 GB of RAM, how many bytes is this?

points: Award 1 mark for working shown
Award 1 mark for correct answer
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Accept scientific notation or full number

scenario: Text is stored using character encoding
question: What does ASCII stand for?
options: A) American Standard Code for Information Interchange
B) Australian System Computer Interface Code
C) Application System Code and Interchange
guidance: Students should know character encoding standards

points: A - American Standard Code for Information Interchange
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Standard 7-bit character encoding

scenario: Extended ASCII allows more characters than standard ASCII
question: Explain why Extended ASCII was developed and what it provides.

points: Standard ASCII limited to 128 characters (7-bit)
Extended ASCII expanded to 256 characters (8-bit)
Provides special characters, symbols, accented letters
Allows support for non-English languages
Includes graphics and box-drawing characters
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on limitation solved and characters added

scenario: Unicode supports all world languages
question: What is Unicode and why is it important for global applications?

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for definition, 1 for importance
points: Definition: Universal character encoding supporting all languages
Supports: Over 1.1 million characters from all scripts
Importance: Enables global communication and software
Importance: Supports Chinese, Arabic, Emoji, etc.
Importance: Standard for modern applications
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on global language support
mark_scheme.do_not_accept: 'Supports many characters' without explaining global aspect

scenario: Operating system manages computer resources
question: Which of these is a key function of the operating system?
options: B) Manage hardware resources and run applications
guidance: Students should know OS primary functions

points: B - OS manages resources and provides platform for applications
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Core OS responsibility

scenario: Operating system manages RAM allocation
question: Describe how the operating system manages computer memory.
guidance: Should explain memory allocation and management

points: Allocates RAM to running programs
Deallocates memory when programs close
Uses virtual memory to extend RAM using disk
Prevents programs accessing other programs' memory
Manages memory pages and segments
Optimizes memory usage for performance
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on allocation, deallocation, and protection aspects

scenario: Operating system organizes file storage
question: What file management functions does the operating system provide?

points: Creates, opens, reads, writes, and deletes files
Organizes files in folders and directories
Manages file permissions and access control
Allocates disk space to files
Tracks file locations on disk
Backs up file system
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Accept any two relevant file management functions

scenario: Operating system communicates with hardware devices
question: What does the OS use to communicate with hardware devices?
guidance: Students should know device driver role

points: A - Device drivers are software that control hardware
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Drivers translate OS commands to device-specific actions

scenario: Operating system runs multiple programs simultaneously
question: How does the OS enable multiple programs to run at the same time?

points: Uses time-slicing to rapidly switch between programs
Allocates CPU time to each process in turn
Context switching stores/restores program state
User perceives simultaneous operation
Scheduler determines which process runs when
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on time-slicing and rapid switching

scenario: Modern computers use graphical user interfaces
question: What does GUI stand for?

points: B - Graphical User Interface using visual elements
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Modern standard interface

scenario: Some systems use text-based command line interfaces
question: What is a command-line interface and describe how it differs from GUI.

points: CLI: Text-based interface using typed commands
GUI: Visual interface with icons, buttons, menus
CLI: Requires knowledge of commands
GUI: Intuitive for most users
CLI: Faster for expert users
CLI: Still used for system administration
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on text-based vs visual as key difference

scenario: GUI uses visual elements for interaction
question: Describe two GUI elements and explain what they do.
guidance: Should identify and explain GUI components

points: Icon: Visual symbol representing file, program, or action
Button: Clickable element performing action when clicked
Menu: List of options user can select from
Window: Container displaying program content
Text box: Input field where user types text
Scroll bar: Controls what portion of content is visible
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Award marks for identifying two elements and explaining purpose
mark_scheme.do_not_accept: Just 'part of GUI' without explaining function

scenario: Different software types serve different purposes
question: Explain the difference between system software and application software.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark per software type explained
points: System software: Manages computer resources and hardware
Application software: Performs specific user tasks
System software includes: OS, drivers, utilities
Application software includes: Word, Excel, browsers
System software is essential for computer operation
Application software is optional based on needs
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on function (resource management vs task specific)

scenario: System maintenance uses utility software
question: Which of these is a utility software?
guidance: Students should know utility software examples

points: B - Disk defragmenter is system utility software
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Utilities optimize and maintain computer

scenario: Various utilities optimize computer performance
question: Describe two types of utility software and their purpose.

points: Disk defragmenter: Reorganizes disk data for faster access
Antivirus: Detects and removes malware
Firewall: Blocks unauthorized network access
Backup utility: Creates copies of data
Compression utility: Reduces file/folder size
Registry cleaner: Removes unnecessary system data
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Accept any two utilities with explanation of purpose

scenario: Software is available under different licensing arrangements
question: Describe two different software licensing models.

points: Perpetual license: One-time purchase, indefinite use
Subscription: Annual/monthly fee for continued use
Free software: No cost, may have restrictions
Freeware: Free to use but copyright retained
Open source: Source code available for modification
Trial: Limited time or feature version
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Accept any two distinct licensing models

scenario: Determining system memory requirements
question: A video file is 700 MB and user has 2 GB of free disk space. How many complete copies can be stored?

points: Convert 2 GB to MB: 2 × 1024 = 2048 MB
Answer: 2 complete copies (rounded down)
Award 1 mark for conversion/working
Award 1 mark for correct answer
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Accept 1000 conversion if clearly stated

scenario: CPU must execute instructions efficiently
question: Explain the fetch-execute cycle and describe what happens at each stage.

points: Fetch: Retrieves instruction from memory address
Decode: Control Unit interprets instruction meaning
Execute: ALU performs operation if needed
Store: Result written back to memory/register
Repeat: Processor continues with next instruction
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Award up to 3 marks for clear explanation of stages

scenario: Modern CPUs have multiple cores
question: What is a multi-core processor and what advantage does it provide?

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for definition, 1 for advantage
points: Definition: Processor with multiple independent processing units
Advantage: Can execute multiple instructions simultaneously
Advantage: Better performance for multitasking
Advantage: Parallel processing capabilities
Each core can run different thread/process
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on simultaneous processing capability

scenario: Office computers are networked together
question: What is a LAN and describe its typical usage.

points: Definition: Local Area Network covering single building/campus
Usage: Connects computers within office/school
Usage: Enables file sharing and resource sharing
Usage: Relatively high speed connections
Typically uses Ethernet cables or WiFi
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on local scope and office/campus context

scenario: Company connects offices across countries
question: What type of network connects locations in different cities or countries?
guidance: Students should distinguish network types by scope

points: C - WAN (Wide Area Network) for large geographic areas
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Internet is largest WAN example

scenario: Personal devices connect wirelessly
question: What is a PAN (Personal Area Network) and give an example?
guidance: Should define and provide relevant example

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for definition, 1 for example
points: Definition: Network covering small personal area (few meters)
Example: Bluetooth connection between phone and headphones
Example: Phone connected to smartwatch
Example: Printer connected to laptop via Bluetooth
Example: Synchronizing devices together
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Accept any personal device connection example

scenario: Network cable connects computer to switch
question: What is the most common type of network cable used in LANs?
guidance: Students should know common network media

points: B - Twisted pair (UTP or STP) is standard LAN cable
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Also called Ethernet cable

scenario: Older systems may use coaxial cables
question: Describe coaxial cable and where it is commonly used.

points: Structure: Central conductor surrounded by shielding
Usage: Cable TV and cable modem connections
Usage: Older computer networks (less common now)
Advantage: Better shielded than twisted pair
Disadvantage: Bulkier, lower bandwidth
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on structure and TV/cable modem use

scenario: Wireless internet access in buildings
question: Describe how WiFi enables wireless network connections.

points: Uses radio waves to transmit data wirelessly
Operates on 2.4 GHz or 5 GHz frequency
Access point broadcasts signal for devices to connect
Enables mobile device connectivity
Range typically 50-100 meters
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on radio wave transmission and device connectivity

scenario: Wireless headphones use Bluetooth
question: What is Bluetooth used for?

points: C - Bluetooth for short-range wireless (typically 10-100 meters)
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Common in phones, headphones, speakers

scenario: Computers can be arranged in different network patterns
question: What is a network topology and describe two types.
guidance: Should define and identify topology types

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for definition, 1 per topology
points: Definition: Physical or logical arrangement of network devices
Star topology: All devices connected to central hub/switch
Ring topology: Devices form circle with data passing around
Bus topology: Devices share single main cable
Mesh topology: Multiple connections between devices
Advantages/disadvantages of each arrangement
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Award marks for definition and two topology types
mark_scheme.do_not_accept: 'How computers connect' without topology type names

scenario: Device directs data between networks
question: What does a router do in a network?

points: B - Router directs data packets between networks
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Uses IP addresses to determine best path

scenario: Switch connects multiple devices in a LAN
question: What is a network switch and how does it differ from a router?
guidance: Should explain switch function and difference

points: Switch: Connects devices within single LAN
Router: Connects different networks together
Switch: Uses MAC addresses
Router: Uses IP addresses
Switch: Operates within local network only
Router: Routes between networks
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on scope difference (local vs between networks)

scenario: Device connects computer to internet service
question: What does a modem do?
options: C) Converts between analog and digital signals

points: C - Modem converts between analog (phone/cable) and digital signals
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Modulation/demodulation device

scenario: Devices need unique network addresses
question: What is an IP address and why is it necessary?

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for definition, 1 for purpose
points: Definition: Unique numerical identifier for each device on network
Purpose: Enables routing of data to correct device
Purpose: Ensures data reaches intended recipient
Format: IPv4 (xxx.xxx.xxx.xxx) or IPv6
Like postal address for network packets
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on identification and routing purpose

scenario: Automatic IP address assignment
question: What does DHCP do and why is it useful?

points: DHCP: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol
Function: Automatically assigns IP addresses to devices
Useful: No manual configuration needed
Useful: Reuses addresses when devices disconnect
Useful: Simplifies network management
Typical in home networks and LANs
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on automation and ease of use

scenario: Network speed is described in bandwidth
question: What does bandwidth measure in a network?

points: B - Bandwidth is maximum data transmission rate
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Measured in bits per second (Mbps, Gbps)

scenario: Network delay affects user experience
question: What is network latency and how does it affect users?

points: Latency: Delay time for data to travel from source to destination
Measured in milliseconds
Effects: Slow response times, lag in gaming/video calls
Effects: Frustrating user experience for time-sensitive apps
Lower latency is better for interactive applications
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on delay and user experience impact

scenario: Actual data transfer speed differs from bandwidth
question: What is throughput and how does it differ from bandwidth?
guidance: Should contrast theoretical vs practical speeds

points: Bandwidth: Theoretical maximum speed
Throughput: Actual speed achieved in practice
Throughput less than bandwidth due to: Overhead, interference, congestion
Throughput affected by: Distance, obstacles, network load
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on theory vs practice difference
mark_scheme.do_not_accept: 'Bandwidth and throughput are same' or only stating definitions

scenario: Data transfer follows agreed rules
question: What is a network protocol?
options: B) Set of rules for data transmission

points: B - Protocol is agreed set of rules for communication
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Examples: TCP/IP, HTTP, FTP

scenario: Internet relies on TCP/IP protocol suite
question: What is TCP/IP and explain why it's important for internet communication?

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for definition, 1 for importance
points: Definition: Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol
TCP: Ensures reliable data delivery and ordering
IP: Handles routing of data packets
Importance: Standard protocol for internet communication
Importance: Enables worldwide connectivity
Universally adopted standard
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Award marks for definition and role explanation

scenario: Converting domain names to IP addresses
question: What does DNS stand for and what does it do?

points: B - DNS converts domain names (like google.com) to IP addresses
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Essential for web browsing

scenario: Secure remote access to network
question: What is a VPN and why might a business use it?
guidance: Should explain and give business use case

mark_scheme.instruction: Award 1 mark for definition, 1 for use case
points: Definition: Virtual Private Network creates secure encrypted connection
Use: Remote workers accessing company network securely
Use: Protecting privacy on public WiFi
Use: Bypassing geographic restrictions
Encrypts all traffic through secure tunnel
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on security and remote access benefit

scenario: Data is broken into packets for transmission
question: What is packet switching and how does it work?
guidance: Should explain packet concept and routing

points: Breaks data into small packets with destination address
Each packet routes independently through network
Packets may take different paths
Reassembled at destination in correct order
Efficient use of network resources
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on breaking up data and independent routing
mark_scheme.do_not_accept: 'Data is sent' without explaining packet mechanism

scenario: Internet and Web are related but different
question: Explain the difference between the Internet and the World Wide Web.

points: Internet: Global network of interconnected computers
Web: Service running on internet using HTTP/HTTPS
Internet: Infrastructure/hardware system
Web: Application layer service
Internet: Supports email, FTP, web, etc.
Web: Only one service on internet
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Focus on infrastructure vs application distinction

scenario: Business considers adopting cloud storage for all documents
question: Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of using cloud storage for business data. Consider security, accessibility, cost, and vendor dependency.

mark_scheme.instruction: Award marks based on balanced discussion

levels.description: Identifies some benefits or drawbacks (easy access, cost) but lacks depth or balance
Explains several advantages (access, backups, scalability) and disadvantages (security, dependency); considers some business implications
Comprehensive discussion of multiple advantages and disadvantages with balanced perspective; addresses business, security, and operational concerns

points: Advantages: Access from anywhere with internet connection
Advantages: Automatic backups and disaster recovery
Advantages: Scalable storage without physical hardware
Advantages: Lower infrastructure costs
Advantages: Easier collaboration and file sharing
Disadvantages: Security/privacy concerns with third party
Disadvantages: Vendor lock-in and dependency
Disadvantages: Internet access required
Disadvantages: Ongoing subscription costs
Disadvantages: Data breach risk with cloud provider
mark_scheme.additional_guidance: Credit analysis of tradeoffs and business impact
mark_scheme.do_not_accept: Only listing pros or cons without balance
